drafted_from: tool:keep-a-stripe-event's own row (its words and input schema) and test/keep-a-stripe-event.test.ts, which runs it on a real Postgres as a login holding exactly read-data/writer-rights.json; read it before relying on it
start_here: Say to your AI: "Keep this Stripe webhook call in bakery_for_who_runs_it, once", with {"payload": "{\"id\":\"evt_sample0101\",\"object\":\"event\",\"type\":\"checkout.session.completed\",\"created\":1793750400,\"data\":{\"object\":{\"id\":\"cs_test_sample0102\",\"object\":\"checkout.session\",\"amount_total\":2500,\"currency\":\"usd\",\"payment_intent\":\"pi_test_sample0103\",\"payment_status\":\"paid\",\"metadata\":{\"offer_id\":\"offer:sample-cake\"}}}}", "signature_header": "t=1793750400,v1=<the signature Stripe sent>", "database": "bakery_for_who_runs_it", "use": {"purpose": "keep-payments", "surface": "site/bakery.example"}, "webhook_secret_name": "bakery-stripe-webhook-signing-secret"}. It runs tool:keep-a-stripe-event and answers {"admitted": true, "event_kind": "payment.confirmed", "id": "payment-event:payment:pi_test_sample0103", "kept": 1}; the same call sent again answers kept 0 with the same id.
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it keeps the payment as one row of the payment_events table in the database you name, the table take-payments payment-keys.ts paymentEventsShape makes, and keeps nothing else.
instructions: 1. Make the payment_events table in your database once (take-payments payment-keys.ts paymentEventsShape: the table and its one-row-per-payment keys), and give your writer login the columns read-data/writer-rights.json names.

2. Point your site's Stripe webhook at an action row that runs tool:keep-a-stripe-event with the raw body ({ "$": "raw_body" }), the stripe-signature header ({ "$": "header", "name": "stripe-signature" }), your database, your site's use and webhook_secret_name, the vault name of the endpoint's signing secret.

3. Read what comes back (the check is tool:check-a-stripe-event's own): admitted false with a reason for a call it did not believe (nothing is kept), or admitted true with the id your store holds for the payment and kept 1 the first time, 0 every time after.
4. Let what follows a payment fire on the new payment_events row (a welcome email, a reward): it is added once, so each follows once.

worked_examples.title: A bakery's paid checkout is kept once
worked_examples.ask: Keep this Stripe webhook call in bakery_for_who_runs_it, once
worked_examples.given: The input {"payload": "{\"id\":\"evt_sample0101\",\"object\":\"event\",\"type\":\"checkout.session.completed\",\"created\":1793750400,\"data\":{\"object\":{\"id\":\"cs_test_sample0102\",\"object\":\"checkout.session\",\"amount_total\":2500,\"currency\":\"usd\",\"payment_intent\":\"pi_test_sample0103\",\"payment_status\":\"paid\",\"metadata\":{\"offer_id\":\"offer:sample-cake\"}}}}", "signature_header": "t=1793750400,v1=<the signature Stripe sent>", "database": "bakery_for_who_runs_it", "use": {"purpose": "keep-payments", "surface": "site/bakery.example"}, "webhook_secret_name": "bakery-stripe-webhook-signing-secret"}, with the signature Stripe sent under the bakery's signing secret.
worked_examples.hands_back: It answered {"admitted": true, "event_kind": "payment.confirmed", "id": "payment-event:payment:pi_test_sample0103", "kept": 1}. The same call again answered {"admitted":true,"event_kind":"payment.confirmed","id":"payment-event:payment:pi_test_sample0103","kept":0}, and a call signed with another secret answered {"admitted":false,"reason":"signature-mismatch","kept":0} with the database never opened.
